edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor changes substrate delivery, microbial competition, short-chain fatty-acid production, or early-life colonization patterns in the gut. Those changes are most directly linked to Inflammatory bowel disease when the endpoint is microbial composition, barrier function, or a gut-mediated immune phenotype.
edges.summary: In children and adolescents, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that early-life antibiotic exposure tracks with higher risk of inflammatory bowel disease. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
